title: Disaster Coming From the North
overview: Jeremiah calls Judah to a real change of heart while warning of a coming invasion and grieving the ruin he sees ahead.

parts.label: What real return looks like (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Turning back to God means throwing out idols and swearing by God's name honestly, and then other nations would want that same blessing. Plowing hard, weedy ground and circumcising the heart are pictures of inner change; circumcision was the physical mark of belonging to God's people, and here it stands for a change on the inside rather than just the outward sign.

parts.label: Warning of invasion (vv. 5-10)
parts.note: Trumpets warn country people to flee into walled cities like Jerusalem because an army is coming from the north, most likely Babylon, pictured as a lion leaving its den. Jeremiah protests that the people were promised peace, probably by prophets who said all was well, though exactly what he means by God deceiving them is debated.

parts.label: Scorching wind, closing army (vv. 11-18)
parts.note: A hot desert wind too strong for sifting grain stands for an army that destroys rather than cleanses, while messengers from Dan in the far north and then the nearer hills of Ephraim show the enemy drawing closer. Jerusalem is urged to wash the evil from its heart, and is told its own choices have brought this on.

parts.label: Jeremiah's anguish (vv. 19-22)
parts.note: Jeremiah, perhaps speaking for the whole nation, cries out as if his heart is pounding at the sounds of war. God answers that his people are skilled at doing wrong but have never learned how to do good.

parts.label: A world undone (vv. 23-28)
parts.note: Jeremiah sees the land as formless and empty, the same words Genesis uses for the world before creation, as if creation itself were being reversed. Yet God says he will not make a complete end, leaving room for some to survive.

parts.label: Jerusalem dressed up and dying (vv. 29-31)
parts.note: As people flee into bushes and rocks, Jerusalem is pictured as a woman putting on makeup and jewels for lovers who now want her dead, probably the foreign allies she had counted on. The chapter ends with her cry, like a woman in her first labor, gasping before her killers.

think: When you have seen trouble coming in your own life or community, what made it hard to change course in time?
